messages.author: 885539f3f5ae8fd5
messages.subject: Missing data
parts:
Hi Phil,

I'm fitting models to data where approximately 20% of the test takers have complete data on all items, 40% have data on the first half of the items and are missing on the second half, and the remaining 40% have data on the second half and are missing on the first half. I've been asked to compare the item parameter estimates when the model is fit to the complete data set where 80% of the test takers having missing data vs. when the model is fit to the test takers who have complete data only. The item parameter estimates I get are quite different under the two scenarios, which doesn't in itself surprise me, but what I found surprising was that under the first scenario with all that missing data the item parameter estimates (particularly the difficulty values) were all rather large and negative. Is this due to all the missing data in that case? When using only the test takers with complete data I got a nice range of positive and negative difficulty estimates. I guess I'm trying to decide if I need to try a second program here or if the results from mirt are indicative enough, on their own, that using a data set with all that missing data just won't work. (I'm really hoping I can conclude that and move on.) Any thoughts would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Jon

messages.author: ab237ff4f31a820f
messages.subject: Re: Missing data
parts:
I know this is addressed to Phil, but I assume you've checked the relative factor scores (aka "ability") of the respondents for any systematic differences? There's a pretty big difference between MCAR and missing by design. Not knowing the particulars of your test design, it's hard to know if this is normal or not. These notes might get you in the direction you want: 

http://web.pdx.edu/~newsomj/semclass/ho_missing.pdf

-Kevin

messages.subject: Re: Missing data
parts:
Hi Phil,

Just wanted to bump this. I'm doing a concurrent calibration on two test forms. Most students complete all 16 items in the two forms. Smaller percentages (say, 20% or less) complete 8 items in one form but not the other 8 items. I'm using the 2PL for all items. mirt gives me very large and negative difficulty parameters when I use this missing-by-design method. If I use ltm, I get roughly the same item parameters as I would get were I to use mirt on the two halves separately. But mirt has all sorts of nice features, like the M2 function, that I can't get using ltm. Do you have any idea why mirt might be having trouble with the large proportion of missing data? Thanks!

- Jon

messages.subject: Re: Missing data
parts:
Hi Jon,

I'm not sure why you'd be obtaining very different parameter estimates use the full vs subset data. Could you provide a reproducible example of this? Missingness should not effect anything in the likelihood functions, so something might be going on in the setup (it sounds like you're in a multiple-group estimation situation). 

Phil
